eligibility.quote: It is sufficient to have a Humble subscriber and do a `ros2 topic list` from Jazzy to (sometimes) trigger the issue.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: a Docker reproducer and observed unbounded memory consumption are public. E2: newer rmw_dds_common discovery definitions reach the older rmw_fastrtps/typesupport consumer across a wire boundary. The malformed-layout handling is not a deployment-name problem. E3: UPGRADE fits newer discovery definitions consumed by Humble-built code; PAIR also describes transport. Stop at 6.

failed_conditions.reason: Agree definition_mismatch: Gid retains its name but its fixed array shrinks. NodeEntitiesInfo contains Gid sequences and ParticipantEntitiesInfo contains Gid and NodeEntitiesInfo, so their serialized definitions change transitively; the failing exchange is discovery, not /chatter.
Agree element_retyped and field:rmw_dds_common/Gid.data. The fixed-array extent changes from 24 to 16 while the field name remains data; this is distinct from the enclosing definition mismatch.

failed_conditions.quote: The crash is triggered by an invalid (excessively large) size argument passed to `resize`.
failed_conditions.reason: Agree other and the two implicated sequence fields. The report traces the allocation at reader_gid_seq.resize and the enclosing ParticipantEntitiesInfo node_entities_info_seq deserializer. This unchecked allocation is an additional defect within the selected composition, not a separate nominal type mismatch.

loudness.quote: The `ros2 topic echo` seems to cause unlimited memory consumption and makes the system run OOM in a matter of seconds.
loudness.reason: Agree silent_documented in S1's stage-limited sense: the documented effect is runtime OOM without an interface-incompatibility refusal at build/connect/activate. Runtime Fast CDR errors and later ASAN analysis do exist; this verdict does not claim total absence of log output.

detection_stage.quote: The `ros2 topic echo` seems to cause unlimited memory consumption and makes the system run OOM in a matter of seconds.
detection_stage.reason: The documented failure is detected at run, not inferred from the location of the eventual edit.

resolution.quote: I've just tested backporting this to Humble, compiling locally and indeed this fixes the issue reported in https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/797
resolution.reason: Agree recommended for the specified composition. This successful experiment uses a Rolling publisher, not the original Jazzy peer, with no exact tested revisions. #828 later confirms Jazzy/Humble reproduction no longer occurs but supplies no fixed package revisions. The diff hardens sequence allocation; it does not make the two discovery definitions identical.

additional_evidence.quote: On the Humble subscriber with a Rolling publisher
After reviewing the patch notes and re-running the reproduction steps, the issue no longer occurs. Thank you.

notes: Read reports #797/#828 and comments, typesupport #130 discussion/diff, Gid change #68 and the three message definitions at 1.6.0 and 3.1.0. Attribution of the discovery-layout incompatibility specifically to the Gid shrink is a code-based inference, not an explicit root-cause sentence in #797. Reader sequence allocation is directly localized in #828. No extra condition is added for every other cross-distro difference or for the unobserved writer allocation path.
